newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says no Freeport comment on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says no Freeport comment on Busang.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Friday that Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc was still conducting its due diligence of the rich Busang gold deposit and had not commented on its progress.

Shares in Bre-X were halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange after a report in Indonesia's Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper that Freeport believed the size of the Busang deposit had been overstated. Bre-X said Freeport officials confirmed "that they are still conducting their due diligence at the Busang site in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, and have not commented on the progress, to the press, in this regard."
Citing an unnamed source, the Indonesian newspaper said Freeport's review of the Busang Two site showed that the gold deposit is lower than Bre-X's estimate of 71 million ounces.

"It is possible that the deposit is not as big as it has been mentioned before. It could be that it is not viable to mine this deposit," Harian Ekonomi Neraca's source said, citing Freeport's results.
However, a Freeport official said on Friday that its due diligence has not been completed.
"We have made no public report. We are not making any report until the due diligence is completed," Freeport vice-president of communications Garland Robinette said in a telephone interview.
Under a recent agreement, New Orleans-based Freeport-McMoRan holds 15 percent of Busang and the right to mine the deposit. Calgary-based Bre-Minerals, which discovered the deposit, has 45 percent.
The rest of Busang is owned by the Indonesian government and two Indonesian companies.
Before it was halted, Bre-X's stock fell 1.20 to 16.25 on 326,000 shares.
Trading in Minorca Resources, which holds a royalty interest in Busang, was also halted on the TSE. Minorca's stock was off 0.55 at 4.80.
